stories.title: Ed Miliband announces first sanctions on Israeli firms working in West Bank
stories.dek: Move is designed to hinder building of more illegal settlements, which Foreign Office says Israel has ‘refused to clamp down on’ UK politics live – latest updates Ed Miliband has announced the first s…
stories.content:
Israeli police stand guard near the settlement of Maale Adummim, in a land corridor known as E1, outside Jerusalem in the occupied West Bank Photograph: Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Israeli police stand guard near the settlement of Maale Adummim, in a land corridor known as E1, outside Jerusalem in the occupied West Bank Photograph: Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty Images West Bank Ed Miliband announces first sanctions on Israeli firms working in West Bank Move is designed to hinder building of more illegal settlements, which Foreign Office says Israel has ‘refused to clamp down on’

Ed Miliband has announced the first set of sanctions against Israeli companies planning to build illegal settlements in the West Bank, after he pledged to try to prevent settlements that destroy the chances of a two-state solution.

The UK foreign secretary also announced he was placing sanctions on a rightwing activist Israeli group involved in trying to block aid into Gaza as recently as last month.

Miliband announced the measures just before tenders for the large E1 West Bank settlement were due to be allocated by the Israeli government, while saying he wanted to work with a new Israeli government in a more cooperative way.

View image in fullscreen Gadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu at the Knesset on 10 November. Photograph: Amir Levy/Getty Images Israel’s possible new prime minister, Gadi Eisenkot has said that, if appointed, he will take a tougher approach than Benjamin Netanyahu to settler violence.

The sanctions are designed to stop the flow of finance to eight identified construction firms, although in practice the extent to which any of the firms are dependent on British finance is yet to be tested.

On 8 September, Miliband announced an expansion of its Global Human Rights sanctions regime, as well as a complex set of measures, yet to be implemented, designed to ban the trade in goods from illegal settlements. The Foreign Office said that it welcomed and encouraged trade with “green line Israel” and firmly distinguished this with activity in settlements.

View image in fullscreen Palestinian children at a makeshift school established inside tents in Gaza City. Photograph: Omar Ashtawy/HL/Getty Images The Foreign Office said the current Israeli government had “not only refused to clamp down on illegal settlement, but has facilitated and encouraged them”. More settlements had been approved under the four years of this Israeli government than in the previous 20 years.

Members of Students Islamic Organisation (SIO) in Telangana were taken into preventive detention over their stance on Telangana government’s Israel-Telangana Strengthening Technology and Business Collaboration at T-Hub in Hyderabad | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

Following the preventative detention of members of Students Islamic Organisation on Monday in Hyderabad , members of civil society accused the police of curtailing democratic right to question the Telangana government’s Israel-Telangana Strengthening Technology and Business Collaboration at T-Hub and called for divestment.

The civil society members said that the detentions were contrary to India’s consistent foreign policy of supporting Palestine. They pointed to what they described as a pattern of targeting educated and successful Muslim youth for raising questions on matters of public interest.

The Telangana police on Monday (November 16, 2026) picked up SIO members soon after civil society members had addressed the media raising serious concerns about the event at T-Hub.

Addressing the media in Hyderabad on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), academic Padmaja Shaw alleged a systematic pattern of targeting educated and successful Muslim youth. Referring to the detention of the SIO members, she said the action appeared intended to send a message that those who spoke out would face police action.

She recalled an earlier incident at the English and Foreign Languages University (EFLU), where female students were picked up over Palestinian literature. She said the police had reacted as though mentioning Palestine was a crime, despite the academic nature of the institution. Ms. Shaw also questioned whether Telangana Police were acting under the influence of the Union government rather than the State government.

While privacy rights activist Srinivas Kodali pointed out that Israeli investment was not new but the time has come to discuss and deliberate on divestment, S Q Masood said most surveillance systems were Israeli technology and efforts must be taken to challenge illegal surveillance in Telangana.

stories.title: Indian woman gang-raped while pregnant in 2002 'heartbroken' after two perpetrators bailed
stories.dek: Bilkis Bano has spoken of her "pain, shock and disbelief" at the top court order and vowed to fight back.
stories.content:
Image source, ANI Image caption, The attack on Bilkis Bano and her family was one of the most horrific crimes during the Gujarat riots

The article has details that some readers may find disturbing

A pregnant Muslim woman who was gang-raped and saw 14 family members murdered during the 2002 Gujarat riots has spoken of her "pain, shock and disbelief" after two of her rapists were recently granted bail.

Bilkis Bano said in a statement that she heard about the top court order through press reports and vowed to fight back.

The freed men are from a group of 11 convicts - part of a Hindu mob - serving life terms for the attack on Bano.

All the men were also freed in 2022 after a Gujarat government order. That decision, and the celebrations as they left prison, caused global outrage . In 2024, the Supreme Court overturned the order .

In a short three-page order dated 28 October, the Supreme Court granted bail to Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya and suspended their sentences while their petition challenging a 2017 Bombay High Court order is being heard.

The judges explained that the early release was because the two convicts "have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years" and "that one of the appellants has a severe handicap".

On Tuesday, Bano's lawyer Shobha Gupta told the BBC that the news of Joshi and Modhiya's release had left "Bilkis heartbroken".

"She has to restart her battle for justice. She had no information that this case was coming up in the Supreme Court. What is troubling for us is that every time something like this happens, we worry that it could affect her faith in judiciary."

Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The riots began after a fire on a passenger train in Godhra town killed 60 Hindu pilgrims

Gupta said it was difficult to understand why the convicts were being released because "it's not a routine criminal case, it's a case that shocks the conscience of the world, of entire humanity".

The attack on Bano and her family was one of the most horrific crimes during the Gujarat riots, which began after 60 Hindu pilgrims were killed in a fire on a passenger train in the town of Godhra.

stories.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
stories.dek: A hidden bug, shifting traffic, and reduced capacity led to cascading failures.
stories.content:
A hidden bug, shifting traffic, and reduced capacity led to cascading failures.

A hidden defect in Microsoft’s cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company’s history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft’s report lists the incident’s final status as “a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents.”

Microsoft’s preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14.

The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft’s cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft’s incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company’s status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report , and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft’s service-health updates .

Microsoft attributes the outage to three factors. A change deployed to Microsoft’s cloud gateway starting in July created a bug where, under certain conditions, CPU and memory resources could become exhausted and unresponsive. Microsoft contends that the defect was never discovered in pre-release testing because the hardware used was less powerful than some systems already deployed in production, where higher CPU core counts on newer machines apparently contributed to the lockout.

The second factor was server load. Microsoft said that “Traffic shifts during standard network maintenance and upgrades exposed a latent bug.” The company keeps two independent gateway systems in place to access Microsoft 365 for resilience. If one system encounters trouble and users can’t get through the front door, the other is opened to keep traffic flowing. According to the report, about 15 hours prior to the outage, traffic from Teams was shifted from the alternate gateway to the primary, where Exchange Online access is maintained. The switchover was a standard fail-safe, but it left the gateway handling more traffic, with a different mix of requests than before. As requests continued to pile up, affected servers exhausted their capacity and refused new connection requests.

stories.title: A material just one atom thick reveals a strange quantum secret
stories.dek: Researchers at the University of Osaka have discovered a remarkable quantum state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal.
stories.content:
Scientists at the University of Osaka in Japan have made a significant discovery in quantum physics, directly observing an unusual electronic state forming where a material just one atom thick meets a metal. Known as a heavy fermion state, this phenomenon causes electrons to behave as though they have much greater mass than normal. These states are associated with extraordinary quantum effects, including unconventional superconductivity, and the discovery could provide a new way to develop materials with unusual electronic properties.

To investigate this behavior, the researchers produced a carefully controlled, single atomic layer of ytterbium and copper (YbCu 2 ) on the surface of a copper crystal. They then used powerful synchrotron light to study the electrons and their interactions at the boundary between the two materials. The results showed that electrons confined to the thin atomic layer could interact with freely moving electrons in the copper beneath it, producing the unusual heavy fermion behavior.

The experiments uncovered two separate heavy fermion states with different characteristics. One existed primarily within the two-dimensional atomic layer, while the other reached beyond that layer and into the three-dimensional copper crystal below.

The second state was particularly important because it provided the first direct evidence of heavy fermion behavior generated by interactions across such an interface. Researchers traced the effect to the mixing, or hybridization, of localized ytterbium 4f electrons in the atomic layer with mobile conduction electrons inside the copper substrate. This interaction demonstrated how combining materials with different electronic characteristics can produce quantum behavior that neither material would necessarily exhibit on its own.

"This achievement was made possible by our continued efforts to create high-quality materials and measure their electronic states as precisely as possible," says senior author Professor Shin-ichi Kimura. "Our next goal is to engineer and control such heavy-electron states, opening the way to previously unexplored quantum states, including unconventional superconductivity."

The discovery suggests that the boundaries between materials could become powerful tools for creating and controlling exotic quantum states. Rather than relying only on the properties of individual substances, scientists may be able to develop entirely new electronic behaviors by carefully selecting and combining ultrathin atomic layers with suitable underlying materials.

Future research could focus on adjusting the structures of these interfaces, controlling the electronic orbitals involved, and manipulating moiré patterns that arise when atomic arrangements overlap. Such approaches may allow researchers to produce and fine-tune quantum phenomena in materials with extremely small dimensions, including effects that cannot be achieved in conventional materials. Ultimately, this could open new possibilities for engineering advanced quantum materials and investigating unconventional superconductivity.

stories.title: Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Agreements and Regional Energy Corridors
stories.dek: A multi-perspective assessment of offshore natural gas transit frameworks, maritime boundary negotiations, and regional stability.
stories.content:
The Eastern Mediterranean basin continues to navigate complex multilateral diplomatic engagements balancing offshore energy exploration with sovereign boundary delimitation. High-level delegations from regional coastal states and European partners are refining frameworks that align pipeline routes with equitable maritime economic zones.

Key Perspectives & Strategic Dimensions:
1. Energy Transit Security: Multilateral agreements between Mediterranean states prioritize uninterrupted transit of natural gas to Southern European ports, diversifying continental supply lines.
2. Maritime Boundary Delimitation: Diplomatic mediators emphasize that long-term maritime stability necessitates transparent dispute-resolution mechanisms that account for sovereign continental shelf claims.
3. Regional Economic Interdependence: Joint infrastructure investments in subsea interconnectors create economic mutual interest, offering pragmatic stabilization incentives across diverse stakeholders.
stories.whyItMatters: Directly impacts the economic stability, energy infrastructure, and security landscape across the Levant and Mediterranean.

stories.title: Sub-Microsecond Spin Dynamics in Diamond NV Centers: Benchmarking Cavity QED and Coherence Limits
stories.dek: Mitigating dipolar spin-spin dephasing and hyperfine bath interactions in dense diamond NV ensembles via Floquet driving.
stories.content:
Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond remain the preeminent solid-state platform for room-temperature quantum metrology and nanoscale magnetic resonance. Scaling from isolated defects to dense ensembles requires overcoming collective dephasing from the surrounding 13C nuclear spin bath.

Recent breakthroughs utilizing microwave cavity coupling and Floquet dynamical decoupling extend the effective coherence time (T2*) by an order of magnitude.

Key Technical Highlights:
1. Cooperative Purcell Enhancement: Dense NV ensembles entering the collective strong coupling regime demonstrate cavity-mediated coherence preservation.
2. Suppression of Spin-Diffusion Loss: Operating within crystallographic symmetry subspaces eliminates cross-axis relaxation.
3. Room-Temperature Sensing: Sustained microsecond coherence enables sub-picotesla magnetic field sensitivities for single-cell NMR.
stories.whyItMatters: Informs room-temperature diamond quantum magnetometry, microwave cavity loading, and advanced Floquet decoupling protocols in spin dynamics.

stories.source: Innatera & Edge AI Insights • 5 min read
stories.title: Sub-Milliwatt Neuromorphic Microcontrollers Shift Real-Time AI Inference to the Edge
stories.dek: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) on silicon processors achieve microsecond response times at sub-milliwatt power budgets.
stories.content:
The paradigm of routing sensor telemetry to centralized cloud servers is rapidly transitioning to on-device neuromorphic microcontrollers. Utilizing event-driven spiking neural architectures, silicon accelerators process acoustic and vibration patterns with near-zero latency.

Key Highlights:
1. In-Memory Processing: Spiking architectures circumvent the classical von Neumann memory bottleneck, consuming less than 1 mW.
2. Zero Cloud Exposure: Sensitive sensor streams remain strictly local, guaranteeing privacy and continuous operation during network blackouts.
3. Predictive Maintenance: Deployed microcontrollers classify industrial vibrations and structural stress in real time.
stories.whyItMatters: Enables zero-latency, private, on-device anomaly detection and vibration monitoring without cloud roundtrips.

stories.title: Circadian Photonic Priming and Equanimity in Demanding Research
stories.dek: Aligning 90-minute ultradian deep work blocks with natural circadian rhythms and secular Buddhist non-reactivity.
stories.content:
Sustained high-level analytical performance requires deliberate biological pacing. Structuring the day around 90-minute ultradian cycles followed by brief decompression intervals prevents cognitive fatigue.

Core Evidence-Based Habits:
1. Photonic Lock: Direct outdoor light exposure within 45 minutes of waking aligns the suprachiasmatic nucleus master clock.
2. Ultradian Block: Dedicate the primary 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM window to pure theoretical derivation before checking correspondence.
3. Secular Equanimity (Dhammapada 81): 'Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.'
stories.whyItMatters: Protects cognitive bandwidth and prevents attentional fragmentation during demanding laboratory derivations.

papers.title: Thermally Activated Magnetic Switching in Antiferromagnetic Van der Waals Trilayers Resolved by Single-Spin Diamond Magnetometry
papers.authors: Fabian A. Gerritsma, Roland W. Mulder, Balázs Nagyfalusi et al.
papers.tldr: Van der Waals magnets provide a versatile platform for exploring magnetic phenomena that emerge from reduced dimensionality, including layer-dependent magnetic ordering. Here, we use scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond magnetometry to measure the magnetization of a trilayer of the A-type antiferromagnet CrPS$_4$, resolving its zero-field bistability between the up-down-up ($\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow$) and down-up-down ($\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow$) layer magnetization configurations.
takeaways: Van der Waals magnets provide a versatile platform for exploring magnetic phenomena that emerge from reduced dimensionality, including layer-dependent magnetic ordering.

Here, we use scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond magnetometry to measure the magnetization of a trilayer of the A-type antiferromagnet CrPS$_4$, resolving its zero-field bistability between the up-down-up ($\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow$) and down-up-down ($\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow$) layer magnetization configurations.

Our results highlight the power of scanning NV magnetometry for the quantitative investigation of magnetization reversal in two-dimensional magnets, unraveling the magnetic phenomenology that emerges in low-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
papers.authors: Chenyang Liao, Chihang Luo, Xin Chen et al.
papers.tldr: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices.
takeaways: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility.
Furthermore, we apply these devices to nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), successfully demonstrating external nanoscale nuclear-spin detection.
These results establish our SiC nanopillars as robust building blocks for scanning quantum probes and scalable sensor networks.

papers.title: Unruh-induced decoherence and entanglement degradation in Ramsey interferometry
papers.authors: E. D. C Brandão, O. P. de Sá Neto, F. C. E. Lima et al.
papers.tldr: We propose a modified Ramsey interferometric protocol to probe decoherence associated with the Unruh effect through fringe visibility. The scheme employs Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum through an interaction that induces pure dephasing without transitions between their internal energy levels.
takeaways: We propose a modified Ramsey interferometric protocol to probe decoherence associated with the Unruh effect through fringe visibility.

The scheme employs Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum through an interaction that induces pure dephasing without transitions between their internal energy levels.
This suggests that the entanglement degradation can be quantified directly from the interference contrast.

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy
papers.authors: Yu-Jie Liu, Richard R. Allen, Ruohan Shen et al.
papers.tldr: Spectroscopy is a versatile tool that drives scientific discovery and underpins modern technologies. Quantum sensing offers promising opportunities to advance spectroscopy through enhanced sensitivity and spectral and spatial resolution.
takeaways: Quantum sensing offers promising opportunities to advance spectroscopy through enhanced sensitivity and spectral and spatial resolution.
Here, we develop an algorithmic approach to quantum sensing tailored to various spectroscopic tasks, providing new avenues for improvement.
For all tasks, we design optimal quantum sensing algorithms achieving a $\sqrt{N}$ speedup over conventional frequency-scanning approaches.

papers.title: Bright-Dark State Interplay Governs Vibronic Decoherence in Molecular Aggregates
papers.authors: Sreeja Loho Choudhury, Abhradeep Sarkar, Raja Ghosh
papers.tldr: In this study, we establish a spectroscopy-driven framework that connects optically bright vibronic eigenstates to their subsequent decoherence dynamics in excitonic molecular aggregates. Combining the Multiparticle Holstein Formalism with explicit system--bath interactions, we demonstrate that relaxation-induced purity loss is governed by three interconnected factors: (i) the bath spectral window, which determines the accessibility of intra- and interband relaxation pathways; (ii) the local network of dark vibronic states surrounding the optically prepared bright state; and (iii) the energetic placement of the bright state, which controls downhill relaxation.
takeaways: In this study, we establish a spectroscopy-driven framework that connects optically bright vibronic eigenstates to their subsequent decoherence dynamics in excitonic molecular aggregates.

Combining the Multiparticle Holstein Formalism with explicit system--bath interactions, we demonstrate that relaxation-induced purity loss is governed by three interconnected factors: (i) the bath spectral window, which determines the accessibility of intra- and interband relaxation pathways; (ii) the local network of dark vibronic states surrounding the optically prepared bright state; and (iii) the energetic placement of the bright state, which controls downhill relaxation.
Remarkably, states with different excitation energies exhibit nearly identical purity dynamics when their local relaxation networks are similar.
